title: a bus-process timeout reaches the asker as a timeout
intention: A timeout inside the bus process reaches the bus_client's caller as a TimeoutError, so a ticket asking a slow chart or verdict gate waits on its own berth instead of dying at the reply timeout.
why: Measured 2026-11-16: 149b9a1ab9c4's walk died at 890 s with 'RuntimeError: bus process: TimeoutError: no reply to envelope 09d15224… from codemother', while codemother's verdict worker (tid 3020324, started 02:38:08 MST) was still re-running its 74 instruments. Ticket.queueme waits on its berth up to 3600 s after a TimeoutError (0bcb816d6e9c), but RemoteBus._call renamed the timeout into a RuntimeError, so the wait never ran and PROVED was refused [hollow_evidence_absent] over work still in progress.
traces_to: Law 7: errors are loud and true at diagnostic surfaces. A timeout renamed into a RuntimeError hid it from the caller built to wait it out.
how: In RemoteBus._call (cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py), beside the LookupError mapping, an error starting 'TimeoutError: ' is raised as TimeoutError with the prefix removed. Every other error keeps its kind.

clauses.claim: a call the bus process answers with 'TimeoutError: <words>' raises TimeoutError whose message is exactly <words>
any other refusal still raises RuntimeError('bus process: ...'), and 'LookupError: ...' still raises LookupError
a request through reach(), from a far client and from a local one, raises TimeoutError when the bus process timed out

decisions.text: D1: RemoteBus._call maps 'TimeoutError: ' back to TimeoutError, beside the LookupError mapping.
D2: a red-first proof replaces remote.exchange (as test_a_far_client_reaches_without_hold.py does), one tooth per clause.
